content: Deploy-observability section in README (warren-c5a5 / pl-7b06 step 20) lives between '### Continuous deployment from GitHub Actions' and '## Power features (opt-in)'. name: prose-guard-degrandfathering
description: check-prose.ts counts sentence fragments PER SOURCE LINE (splitSentences runs on each line independently), so an 80-col-wrapped paragraph accrues ~1 fragment per line toward the long-paragraph(>6s) rule. To de-grandfather a doc from prose-budgets.json, rewrite with semantic line breaks (one sentence per line), paragraphs <=6 lines, and watch that colon+Capital/inline-code mid-line splits add fragments. Passive regex only fires on BE directly followed by a participle ('is not scoped' escapes; ADJECTIVAL list words like set/pinned/permitted are exempt). Tables, headings, and code fences are skipped entirely. Delete the file's budgets entry once it hits 0 — threshold is 0.

content: scripts/check-prose.ts runs splitSentences per PHYSICAL source line. A hard-wrapped 7-line paragraph accrues ~1 fragment per line and trips long-paragraph(>6s) even when it holds only 2 real sentences. Bullet items have the same failure: a wrapped continuation line does not match isList, so it accumulates into the surrounding paragraph and a whole '-' list reads as one 20-sentence block. Fix with semantic line breaks, not rewording.

description: bun install in a fresh git worktree rewrites bun.lock with ~261 lines of unrelated churn
resolution: Run 'git checkout -- bun.lock' before committing. Affects every worktree-based agent run on bun 1.3.14; otherwise the lockfile churn lands as unrelated diff in the PR.

title: prose-budgets.json terminal state is absence, not a smaller number
rationale: Removing the entry pins the doc at threshold 0, so any future edit introducing even one violation fails lint. This is stricter than the allowance it replaces and is the guard's documented design — the ratchet's terminal state for a doc is absence from the budget file.

content: Division of labour across warren's doc surfaces: seeds owns the queue, SPEC.md the design record, CHANGELOG the ship log, PHILOSOPHY.md the sequencing. ROADMAP holds Now / Next / Shipped / Deliberately not in core / Removed and nothing else. Shipped items shrink to one table row linking a version plus a SPEC section; no design sketches land in it. This is what keeps it from re-growing to 91 KB.

description: Seed bodies can go stale mid-plan: warren-9600 listed canopy under Removed, but CANOPY_REPO_URL is still live in handlers/agents.ts, diagnostics.ts and doctor.ts
resolution: Verify a removal claim against the code before writing it into a doc. Canopy was documented as a live optional integration instead. On a long plan the seed body is a snapshot of planning-time belief, not current truth.

content: Two reading paths: newcomer (README -> project-setup -> RUNBOOK-K8S) and contributor (CONTRIBUTING -> labels -> http-api -> CONSTITUTION), plus a one-line purpose per remaining doc. CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md #Development both point at it. Adding a doc under docs/ without a row there makes it unreachable.

Format: a blockquote 'HISTORICAL — shipped in vX.Y.Z' naming the live doc that replaced it. Applied to k8s-migration.md and runtime-provider-contract.md. Prevents an agent reading a shipped design doc as a live plan, which is how ROADMAP.md drifted for two months.

name: doc-deletion-checklist
description: Deleting a doc: grep the whole repo for inbound links first — a deleted doc that is still linked is worse than a stale doc

content: scripts/check-prose.ts's long-paragraph(>6s) rule effectively counts wrapped LINES: every non-empty prose line contributes >=1 fragment, plus one per mid-line sentence split (splitSentences breaks on [.!?:] + whitespace + uppercase). AGENTS.md is grandfathered at exactly its 35-violation ceiling, so any prose added to it must keep each touched paragraph at <=6 wrapped lines and place sentence boundaries at line ends (or split into a new paragraph). Verify the count before committing: bun -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {lint, countable} from "./scripts/check-prose.ts"; console.log(countable(lint(readFileSync("AGENTS.md","utf8"),25).violations).length)' — must stay <=35. Mirroring an existing passing sentence's wording (e.g. the gen:docs:check bullet) is the safest way to add bullets at zero new violations.
